clue.text: Pictures, poem and book as human creations

parts.note: pictures as a whole are art
If is Kipling's famous poem
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Paintings, verse and literature celebrated as the great works of mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Artefacts are objects made by people, as opposed to natural things.

clue.text: Notice amount of money needed for present!

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Advertisement fees must be paid before a present can be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word answered at a roll-call means 'I am here'.
explanation.definitionFit: At a roll-call the Latin reply meaning 'I am here' is the equivalent of calling out that you are in attendance.

clue.text: Scrap some fine material

parts.note: a scrap is a quarrel, a tiff
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Throw away a bit of the good fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany is a thin, gauzy silk muslin.

clue.text: Products of mine used in battle as aid to marksmanship

indicators.note: the mined products are placed inside the word for battle

parts.note: a battle is a fight
ores are what a mine produces

explanation.surface: Minerals dug up are put to use in war to help gunners hit targets.
explanation.definitionFit: The foresight is the sight at the muzzle end of a gun barrel, lined up when aiming.

clue.text: Change, for instance? Not for the emperor

definitions.text: Change, for instance? Not for the emperor

parts.words: Change, for instance? Not for the emperor
parts.note: the Roman emperor's name begins with a word meaning unchanging, so change is the last thing his name suggests

explanation.surface: Reform, perhaps, but not something an emperor would welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The first eight letters of the emperor's name spell a word meaning steady and unchanging, the opposite of 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor who founded Constantinople, whose name opens with a word for steadfast.

clue.text: Stressing beams might, centrally, produce this

definitions.text: Stressing beams might, centrally, produce this

indicators.note: the middle letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: Putting stress on beams can make them droop in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaded beam bends and dips in the middle, a downward droop.

clue.text: Animal without fleece, a half-wild creature

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the animal surrounds the swindle

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
to fleece is to swindle, to do someone

explanation.surface: A beast without its woolly coat, a creature only partly tame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like the wool, but it is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah dog is a stray, semi-feral ownerless dog of Asia.

clue.text: Vegetarian item taken for medical reasons

explanation.surface: A meatless dish swallowed on doctor's orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils and beans are pulses, staples of meatless cooking; a doctor takes your heartbeat rate by feeling the wrist.

clue.text: Her fettered lover was unlocked

parts.note: the biblical temptress had her lover's hair cut off, leaving him bound in chains: unlocked means shorn of his locks, not released

explanation.surface: A woman whose chained partner was set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlocked' seems to mean freed from his fetters, but it means his locks of hair were cut: the story of Samson.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges the Philistine woman betrayed Samson by having his hair shorn, after which he was captured and chained.

clue.text: Nothing on chart is concealed in Scot's great layout

indicators.note: the zero and chart sit inside the Scots word

parts.note: gey is a Scots word for very great or considerable

indicators.note: in a down clue the zero sits on top of the chart

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A blank map hidden in a Scotsman's grand plan.
explanation.walkthrough: GEY is Scottish dialect for great or very.
explanation.definitionFit: The physical arrangement of a place or region, its lie of the land, can be called its geography.

clue.text: Bloomer made by son, little short of an insult

indicators.note: the word for an insult is cut by its last letter

parts.note: an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by a son, almost an outright insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower; 'little short of' drops the T from AFFRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and the autumn crocus yielding the spice is one.

clue.text: Astronomer showing girl one constellation

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one
Leo, the Lion, is a constellation

explanation.surface: A stargazer pointing out a group of stars to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist who championed the telescope and discovered Jupiter's moons.

clue.text: Money for imports

explanation.surface: Cash spent on foreign goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's wealth or resources are their wherewithal; to signify something is what imports does as a verb.

clue.text: Representative who shouldn't be narrow-minded?

parts.note: a commercial sales representative is always on the road, and travel is said to broaden the mind

explanation.surface: A delegate who ought to have broad views.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'travel broadens the mind' lies behind the question.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a salesman who journeys round visiting customers.

clue.text: Short work made of a game people finish off fast

parts.note: bridge is a card game
men are people

indicators.note: the final letter of the word fast is taken

explanation.surface: A brief piece created out of a match that players end quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged version of a book is a shortened edition of it.

clue.text: Believe what's overheard?

parts.note: accepting a story you have been told, slangily, is to purchase it

explanation.surface: Should you trust what you hear by chance?
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a claim as true, slangily, is to purchase it, as in 'I don't buy that'.

clue.text: Attacking creature outside burrow

indicators.note: the creature goes round the burrow

parts.note: a being is a creature
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: An animal hunting around a hole in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A besetting sin is one that constantly assails or harasses you.

clue.text: Imprecise craft, the art of command

parts.note: general means vague, imprecise
a ship is a craft

explanation.surface: A vague vessel, and the skill of leading troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Generalship is military leadership, the skill of a commanding officer.

clue.text: Noblewoman and economist invested in South Africa

parts.note: a lady is a noblewoman
Adam Smith was the Scottish economist

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and a financial expert putting money into South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' means besieged, not putting money in: the town in Natal was besieged in the Boer War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Natal town was famously surrounded by Boer forces for four months in 1899-1900.

clue.text: Unable to stay terse?

explanation.surface: Too brief to hang around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking puff, someone breathless cannot keep going; and curt, brief speech is the same word used figuratively.

clue.text: View showing duck on the wing.

indicators.note: in a down clue the duck sits on top of the wing

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: Seeing a duck in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief or judgement held by someone is their point of view.

clue.text: Philanthropist's down-to earth supporter

explanation.surface: A benefactor's grounded backer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Guy founded Guy's Hospital in London; a rope pegged into the ground holds up a tent.

clue.text: Inspired work of art calls for celebration drink

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A great painting demands a party with refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: Pygmalion's statue was brought to life, given breath, which is the literal sense of 'inspired'.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the sculptor Pygmalion's ivory statue was granted life by Aphrodite.

clue.text: Part of instrument Meg lost in night flight

explanation.surface: A violin component that a woman lost while escaping at night.
explanation.walkthrough: In Burns's poem Tam o' Shanter, Tam's mare Meg loses her tail to a witch as they flee by night.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin the strings are anchored at the lower end to this fitting; and Meg's tail came off in the chase.

clue.text: Bodily balance I required in model

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the word for model

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: Grace of carriage is something I need when modelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is graceful, steady carriage of the body.

clue.text: Musical direction, supposedly, brings second sound back

indicators.note: the word for sound is read backwards

parts.note: sound means healthy, hale

explanation.surface: A musical instruction brings a second note in again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is the adjective meaning healthy, not a noise; 'back' turns HALE into ELAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The word in the Psalms is thought, though uncertainly, to be an instruction to the musicians, perhaps a pause.

clue.text: Lexicographer's pet name for countryman

explanation.surface: A dictionary-writer's favourite term for a rustic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Johnson, maker of the Dictionary, had a cat of that name; it is also a traditional English name for a farm labourer.

clue.text: First sign, in brief

explanation.surface: The earliest indication, put shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means coming at the start; to sign with just the first letters of your names is to sign in brief.

clue.text: Grass cut short, as a rule

indicators.note: the word for grass loses its last letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: Grass is normally mown.
explanation.definitionFit: A law is a rule laid down.

clue.text: Was left without a shilling

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for left goes round the shilling

parts.note: exited means left
S is the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: Someone departed with no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been in being is past tense of to be: a form of 'was'.

clue.text: Green bananas — the French kind

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Unripe fruit, of the type grown in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for kind or type is used in English for a category of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Genre is a French borrowing meaning type or sort, used for categories of art.

clue.text: Observe situation providing cover for hunter

parts.note: to observe is to watch
a case is a situation or state of affairs

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on the position gives shelter to someone hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged metal lid protecting its face.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch whose glass is shielded by a metal lid, so its outer shell is the cover.
